articles.headline: containerd 2.4.0 lands with dual binaries and a longer support window
articles.dek: The 13th containerd release adds a static binary option, bumps the API to v1.12.0, and promises an extended lifecycle for stability‑focused users.

body.text: Key Takeaway

containerd 2.4.0 ships both a dynamically linked Ubuntu build and a statically linked binary, and it extends the supported lifecycle—so you can avoid glibc version mismatches and skip frequent version churn. [FACT:241a8ae738936bdfaddf7062117c5443] [FACT:067f988ac99db781ac7df06c6867c86e] [FACT:882fad2eda0671782dda004832f9fbd5]
Why This Matters

Kubernetes nodes still use containerd as the default OCI runtime; the new static binary removes the glibc version lock that trips up Alpine‑based nodes, and the longer support window reduces upgrade noise for teams that lock versions for stability. [FACT:067f988ac99db781ac7df06c6867c86e] [FACT:241a8ae738936bdfaddf7062117c5443] [FACT:882fad2eda0671782dda004832f9fbd5]
What Happened

Version 2.4.0 is the 13th major release of containerd and includes API v1.12.0, officially recommended tarballs for common architectures, and is labelled a regular (non‑preview) release. [FACT:ea7de698708c98012388df730050255b] [FACT:1b5c302efa88acf69ff953cf2e8ad010] [FACT:e0f34550ad17659dd9a6053cdc772929]
Builder View

If your clusters run Ubuntu, stick with the dynamically linked tarball; if you target Alpine or other minimal distros, pull the static tarball to sidestep the glibc dependency. Validate the new API 1.12.0 against your Kubelet before promoting to production. [FACT:241a8ae738936bdfaddf7062117c5443] [FACT:067f988ac99db781ac7df06c6867c86e] [FACT:ea7de698708c98012388df730050255b]

articles.headline: datasette 1.0a40 drops a security patch and flips to httpx2
articles.dek: The latest prerelease of datasette adds the same security fix as the last update and migrates its internal HTTP client to httpx‑2.

body.text: Key Takeaway

datasette 1.0a40 ships a security fix that mirrors the one in the previous 0a40 release and swaps the internal HTTP stack to httpx2, so your instances stay safe and gain a more modern networking layer [FACT:91560b90925871d8aa8da93f1afe6a83][FACT:b5f103f9b70585d51f15f19faa4a1851].
